STATUS: ADOPTED -- reinstated 2026-08-28 after the retraction was itself withdrawn

retraction.why: contradicted by two independent instruments that agree with each other: the DoD on stable open ground (-2.12 mm, 116,507 cells) and the leveled benchmark DG8385 (gen2-gen1 = +73.00 +/- 11.00 mm raw, predicting +5.62 mm after the pipeline's +67.38 mm geoid shift). Those two agree to 7.74 mm; this value implies ~+65 mm.
retraction.what_is_wrong: not the measurement -- our ties match the vendor's own published residuals at the same marks to -6.71 mm. The 8 open marks on Elba's lines sit +54.46 mm above the 230-mark open population and are dominated by control 14-63 km away; the two marks inside 10 km give +17.20 mm and the nearest gives -11.3 mm.
retraction.conclusion: the absolute level of gen1 at Elba is NOT measurable with the available control; the EPOCH DIFFERENCE is settled to ~8 mm by two instruments.

retraction_withdrawn.the_retraction_was_wrong: it rested on my own algebra error: I asserted the geoid cancels between c1 and c2. It does not. NAVD88 is the DATUM; GEOID03/GEOID18 are MODELS for converting GPS ellipsoidal heights to orthometric. Both control sets publish NAVD88 and are directly comparable, but the LIDAR z of each epoch was converted with a different geoid model, so c1 and c2 reference surfaces in different frames. The correct relation is DoD = c1 - c2 - g.
retraction_withdrawn.implication: nothing was contradicted. c1_ours=+58.70 and c2=-6.56 are both correct, gen2's bridge is ~0, and the DoD, the benchmark DG8385 and the control all agree.

dod_absolute_correction_note: gen1 sits in the DoD AFTER the +67.38 geoid shift, so its constant there is c1_ours - g = -8.68 mm. DoD correction = c2 - c1_pipe = +2.12 mm, and applying it puts stable open ground at -0.00 mm.
